about: The inside of the small intestine, drawn as anatomy: its three regions (duodenum, jejunum and ileum) inside a muscular wall, the circular folds, the string of chyme in the lumen, the Peyer's patches of the ileum, the ileocaecal junction, and the mesenteric arteries and veins. One short stretch of jejunal mucosa is drawn opened out and ENLARGED, with its villi, capillary loops and central lacteals, because the real villi are far too small to see at the scale of the bowel. It leaves out the mesentery as a membrane, the crypts, the enteric nerve plexuses, the brush border and every secretory and enzymatic detail. Chyme moves along the lumen with the model's peristalsis, absorbed nutrients leave the mucosa towards the portal vein at the rate the engine reports for glucose absorption, and lymph appears in the lacteals when fat is in the upper gut. Activity bars are display indices, not measurements. The four parts of the duodenum, its papillae, the wall layers, the plexuses and the cells of one enlarged villus and crypt are drawn as finer structures; the villus and crypt are enlarged many times and cell counts are schematic.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Duodenum
parts.summary: First part of the small bowel; receives stomach contents, bile and pancreatic juice
parts.function: The duodenum is the short, wide first region of the small intestine. Chyme from the stomach is neutralised here, and bile and pancreatic juice join it at the major duodenal papilla, which is where most chemical digestion begins. Fat arriving in it triggers the hormonal signals that release bile and slow the stomach. In this simulator it brightens when food reaches the upper gut.

drives.note: Food in the stomach and upper bowel means chyme is arriving here to be mixed with bile and pancreatic juice.
Fat in the duodenum is the stimulus for bile release and for slowing gastric emptying.
Vagal outflow raises secretion and motility in the upper gut.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits small-bowel motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale (as muscular_wall), not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Jejunum
parts.summary: Middle region; the main site of nutrient absorption, with the densest folds
parts.function: The jejunum is the middle region of the small bowel, with the tallest and most closely set circular folds and the most villi. Most sugars, amino acids and fats are absorbed here. It brightens when the engine reports glucose entering the portal blood and when contents are passing through the small bowel.

drives.note: The jejunum is the principal absorbing region, so it follows the absorption signal.
Digestion in the upper gut sends chyme on into the jejunum.
Contents in the small bowel mean the region is working.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits small-bowel motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale (as muscular_wall), not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Ileum
parts.summary: Last region; absorbs bile salts and vitamin B12 and carries the Peyer's patches
parts.function: The ileum is the final, narrower region of the small intestine. It absorbs what the jejunum left, including bile salts, which are returned to the liver, and it has the lymphoid Peyer's patches in its wall. It ends at the ileocaecal junction. It brightens with transit of contents and with gut motility.

drives.note: Chyme that has passed the jejunum arrives here.
The ileum absorbs the remainder of the nutrient load.
Raised gut motility drives chyme through the ileum faster.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits small-bowel motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale (as muscular_wall), not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Muscular Wall
parts.summary: Circular and longitudinal smooth muscle that mixes and propels the chyme
parts.function: The wall of the small intestine has an inner circular and an outer longitudinal layer of smooth muscle. Segmenting contractions mix the chyme with digestive juices, and peristaltic waves move it on towards the colon. Vagal activity increases this muscle's work and sympathetic activity reduces it. In this simulator it brightens with motility and vagal outflow and dims with sympathetic outflow.

drives.note: Drugs or states that raise gut motility act on this muscle.
Reduced motility, for example from opioids, quietens the muscle.
Vagal outflow excites intestinal smooth muscle.
Sympathetic outflow inhibits intestinal motility.

parts.label: Chyme in the Lumen
parts.summary: The partly digested food mixture, drawn as a segmented string of boluses
parts.function: Chyme is the semi-fluid mixture of food, gastric and pancreatic juice and bile that passes along the lumen. Segmenting contractions divide it into short portions, which is why it is drawn as a string of boluses with constrictions between them. It brightens with the amount of material in the small bowel and with motility.

drives.note: More material in the small bowel means more chyme to show.
Digestion in the upper gut is what supplies chyme.
Faster motility carries chyme through more quickly.

parts.label: Circular Folds
parts.summary: Permanent folds of mucosa and submucosa; closest together in the jejunum
parts.function: The plicae circulares, or valvulae conniventes, are permanent circular folds of the mucosa and submucosa that project into the lumen. They increase the surface available for absorption and slow the passage of chyme. They are close together in the duodenum and jejunum and sparse and low in the ileum. They brighten with absorption.

drives.note: The folds carry the absorbing surface, so they follow the absorption signal.
Digestion in the upper gut is what gives them something to absorb.

parts.label: Mucosa with Villi
parts.summary: Absorbing lining; one stretch drawn opened out and enlarged
parts.function: The mucosa is the absorbing lining of the bowel. Its finger-like villi, and the microvilli on their cells, multiply the surface in contact with the chyme. Each villus has a capillary network that takes up sugars and amino acids into the portal blood. The stretch drawn here is opened out and ENLARGED so the villi can be seen; it is not at the scale of the bowel. It brightens with the glucose absorption the engine reports.

drives.note: Nutrients crossing the mucosa into the portal blood are what the absorption signal counts.
Digestion supplies the nutrients to absorb.

parts.label: Lacteals
parts.summary: Lymph vessels in each villus that carry absorbed fat away as chyle
parts.function: Each villus has a central blind-ended lymphatic vessel, the lacteal. Absorbed fats, packaged as chylomicrons, enter the lacteals rather than the blood capillaries and travel in the lymph, which looks milky and is called chyle, towards the thoracic duct. In this simulator the lacteals light and their lymph stream appears when there is fat in the upper gut.

drives.note: Fat arriving in the gut is what the lacteals carry away.
A meal in the upper gut precedes fat absorption.

parts.label: Peyer's Patches
parts.summary: Lymphoid follicles in the ileal wall that sample the gut contents
parts.function: Peyer's patches are aggregates of lymphoid follicles in the wall of the ileum, on the side away from the mesentery. They sample material from the lumen and take part in mucosal immunity. They brighten when the simulator reports immune activation or infection.

drives.note: Immune activation raises lymphoid tissue activity.
A pathogen burden engages gut-associated lymphoid tissue.

parts.label: Ileocaecal Junction
parts.summary: Valve at the end of the ileum where it joins the caecum
parts.function: The ileocaecal junction is where the ileum opens into the caecum. Its lips act as a valve that releases chyme into the colon in small portions and resists the backward flow of colonic contents. It brightens with transit of contents and motility.

drives.note: Chyme reaching the end of the ileum is passed through this valve.
Faster motility passes chyme through more often.

parts.label: Mesenteric Arteries and Veins
parts.summary: Arterial arcades bring blood to the bowel; veins carry nutrients to the portal vein
parts.function: The superior mesenteric artery fans into branches and arcades in the mesentery that supply the small bowel. Matching veins collect the blood that has taken up nutrients and join the superior mesenteric vein, which drains into the portal vein and so to the liver. Blood flow to the gut rises after a meal and falls when sympathetic outflow rises. It brightens with digestion and absorption.

drives.note: Gut blood flow rises while food is being digested.
Absorbed nutrients leave the gut in the mesenteric veins.
Sympathetic outflow constricts the splanchnic vessels.

parts.label: Superior Part of the Duodenum
parts.summary: The first part of the duodenum, leaving the stomach
parts.function: The superior part is the short first stretch of the duodenum, which receives chyme from the pylorus. It is where the duodenal glands are most numerous.

drives.note: Chyme arriving from the stomach is mixed here with bile and pancreatic juice.

parts.label: Descending Part of the Duodenum
parts.summary: The second part, running down and receiving bile and pancreatic juice
parts.function: The descending part runs down on the right side of the loop. The bile duct and pancreatic duct open into it at the major duodenal papilla.

drives.note: Chyme arriving from the stomach is mixed here with bile and pancreatic juice.
Fat in the duodenum stimulates bile release.

parts.label: Horizontal Part of the Duodenum
parts.summary: The third part, crossing the midline
parts.function: The horizontal part crosses from right to left, passing below the head of the pancreas and in front of the large vessels behind it.

drives.note: Chyme arriving from the stomach is mixed here with bile and pancreatic juice.

parts.label: Ascending Part of the Duodenum
parts.summary: The fourth part, rising to the duodenojejunal flexure
parts.function: The ascending part climbs on the left of the midline and ends at the duodenojejunal flexure, where the duodenum becomes the jejunum.

drives.note: Chyme arriving from the stomach is mixed here with bile and pancreatic juice.

parts.label: Major Duodenal Papilla
parts.summary: The raised opening where the bile and main pancreatic ducts enter
parts.function: The major duodenal papilla is a small elevation on the inner wall of the descending duodenum. Bile and pancreatic juice pour through it onto the chyme.

drives.note: Fat in the duodenum is the stimulus for bile release.
Digestion in the upper gut calls for bile and pancreatic juice.

parts.label: Minor Duodenal Papilla
parts.summary: A smaller opening above the major papilla, for the accessory pancreatic duct
parts.function: The minor duodenal papilla lies above the major one and is the opening of the accessory pancreatic duct when that duct is present.

drives.note: Digestion in the upper gut calls for pancreatic juice.

parts.label: Duodenal (Brunner) Glands
parts.summary: Mucus-secreting glands in the submucosa of the duodenum
parts.function: Brunner glands release an alkaline mucus that protects the duodenal wall from the acid arriving from the stomach. They are drawn as enlarged flasks, in a sparse scatter.

drives.note: Acid chyme arriving from the stomach stimulates them.
Vagal outflow stimulates their secretion.

parts.label: Duodenojejunal Flexure
parts.summary: The sharp bend where the duodenum becomes the jejunum
parts.function: The duodenojejunal flexure marks the end of the duodenum. It is held in place by the suspensory muscle of the duodenum.

drives.note: Chyme leaving the duodenum passes round it.

parts.label: Suspensory Muscle of the Duodenum (Treitz)
parts.summary: A band of fibromuscular tissue that suspends the duodenojejunal flexure from above
parts.function: The suspensory muscle is a thin band running from the duodenojejunal flexure up toward the region of the coeliac artery. It fixes the flexure and is a landmark that divides the duodenum from the jejunum.

parts.label: Mesentery
parts.summary: The fold of peritoneum that suspends the jejunum and ileum and carries their vessels
parts.function: The mesentery is a double layer of peritoneum that attaches the small bowel to the back wall of the abdomen. It carries the arteries, veins, nerves and lymphatics to and from the bowel. It is drawn as a flat fan, not the real fatty fold.

drives.note: Blood flow through it rises while food is being digested.

parts.label: Submucosal (Meissner) Plexus
parts.summary: The nerve network in the submucosa of the small intestine
parts.function: The submucosal plexus is part of the enteric nervous system. It controls local secretion and blood flow in the mucosa. The braid drawn here is schematic.

drives.note: Vagal fibres connect with the enteric neurons of the plexus.
A meal engages the secretory reflexes of the plexus.

parts.label: Myenteric (Auerbach) Plexus
parts.summary: The nerve network between the two muscle layers
parts.function: The myenteric plexus coordinates the contraction of the muscle coat and so controls the movement of chyme along the bowel. The braid drawn here is schematic.

drives.note: Vagal fibres connect with the enteric neurons of the plexus.
Raised motility engages the enteric nervous system.

parts.label: Serosa
parts.summary: The smooth outer covering of the small intestine, a layer of peritoneum
parts.function: The serosa is the visceral peritoneum covering the bowel. It is slippery, so the coils can slide over one another as they move.

parts.label: Circular Muscle Layer
parts.summary: The inner muscle layer, with fibres running round the bowel
parts.function: The circular fibres narrow the lumen when they contract. Local rings of contraction, segmentation, mix the chyme and bring it against the lining.

drives.note: Drugs or states that raise gut motility act on this muscle.
Reduced motility quietens the muscle.
Vagal outflow excites intestinal smooth muscle.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits small-bowel motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale, not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Longitudinal Muscle Layer
parts.summary: The outer muscle layer, with fibres running along the bowel
parts.function: The longitudinal fibres shorten a length of bowel when they contract. Together with the circular layer they produce the peristaltic wave that moves chyme onward.

drives.note: Drugs or states that raise gut motility act on this muscle.
Reduced motility quietens the muscle.
Vagal outflow excites intestinal smooth muscle.

Sympathetic outflow inhibits small-bowel motility, so this part is drawn BELOW its resting level under sympathetic drive. Sign from the textbook; the weight is a display coupling on this atlas's own scale, not a measured effect size.

parts.label: Villus (enlarged)
parts.summary: One finger-like villus drawn many times larger than those in the patch below
parts.function: A villus is a fold of the lining that increases the surface for absorption. This one is drawn enlarged above the patch so its cells can be seen. Its cells and capillaries are shown as children of the mucosa.

parts.label: Enterocytes (Brush Border)
parts.summary: The absorbing cells of the lining, with a brush border of microvilli
parts.function: Enterocytes are the most numerous cells of the lining. Their free surface is covered by microvilli, the brush border, which increases the area for absorbing nutrients and holds enzymes that finish digestion.

drives.note: Nutrients crossing the lining are absorbed by these cells.

parts.label: Goblet Cells
parts.summary: Mucus-secreting cells scattered among the absorbing cells
parts.function: Goblet cells release mucus onto the surface of the lining, which lubricates the passage of chyme and protects the lining.

drives.note: A meal in the gut stimulates mucus release.

parts.label: Villus Capillaries
parts.summary: Capillary loops in each villus that carry absorbed nutrients away
parts.function: Each villus holds a network of capillaries just under its surface. They take up most absorbed nutrients and carry them toward the liver in the portal vein.

drives.note: Absorbed nutrients leave the gut in these capillaries.
Gut blood flow rises while food is being digested.

parts.label: Intestinal Crypts (of Lieberkühn)
parts.summary: Tubular pits between the villi where the lining renews itself
parts.function: The crypts are simple tubular glands that open between the villi. Stem cells at their base renew the lining, and the cells move up toward the villus tips as they mature.

parts.label: Paneth Cells
parts.summary: Granule-filled cells at the base of the crypts
parts.function: Paneth cells sit at the base of the crypts and release antimicrobial substances that help keep the bacteria of the lumen away from the stem cells.

drives.note: A pathogen burden engages the gut's defences.

parts.label: Enteroendocrine Cells
parts.summary: Scattered cells of the lining that release gut hormones
parts.function: Enteroendocrine cells sense the contents of the lumen and release hormones into the blood that control digestion. Several kinds exist; the I, S and K cells are shown.

drives.note: Food in the gut is what they sense.

parts.label: I Cells (CCK)
parts.summary: Enteroendocrine cells that release cholecystokinin
parts.function: I cells release cholecystokinin in response to fat and protein in the duodenum. It makes the gallbladder contract and the pancreas release enzymes.

drives.note: Fat in the duodenum is the stimulus for CCK release.

parts.label: S Cells (Secretin)
parts.summary: Enteroendocrine cells that release secretin
parts.function: S cells release secretin when acid enters the duodenum. It makes the pancreas and bile ducts release a bicarbonate-rich fluid that neutralises the acid.

parts.label: K Cells (GIP)
parts.summary: Enteroendocrine cells that release glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide
parts.function: K cells release GIP in response to glucose and fat in the upper bowel. It helps the pancreas release insulin in proportion to the meal.

drives.note: Absorbed glucose is a stimulus for GIP release.
Fat is also a stimulus.
